ssl_manager.description: JEC acts as the client of Namecheap's server-side automation (SSL Manager) and gets each certificate of the subscription. When you activate or reissue the certificate in Namecheap's panel, choose Server-side automation and enter the one-time token it shows here. The API is not public and may break at any time.
ssl_manager.name: Namecheap SSL Manager

test.ok: Connected to Namecheap; {count, plural, one {# certificate} other {# certificates}} in sight.

card.no_events: No events chosen: it sends nothing

error.send: The note could not be sent.

module.description: Tells you through the channels you set up when a certificate cannot be issued or deployed, or is about to expire.
module.name: Notifications

expiring.title: The certificate for {domain} {days, plural, =0 {expires today} one {expires in # day} other {expires in # days}}

note.gave_up: JEC will not try again by itself: this needs you.

issue_failed.title: Could not issue the certificate for {domain}

note.served_old: The certificate it serves ends on {served}, the version in use on {current}: the target, such as a CDN, may not have taken the new one.
note.subject: [JEC] {title}

test.sent: The test is on its way.
test.text: If this reached you, the channel is set up right.
test.title: A test note

error.auth: {address} refused {user}: check the user, the key or the password.
error.command: The command failed with status {status}; the log has its output.
error.file_path: The source asked for a file outside /.well-known/, which JEC does not write: {path}
error.host_key: The server's host key is not the one set (it showed {fingerprint}). If the server was reinstalled, update the setting; otherwise someone may pose as it, so hold off.
error.host_key_unknown: The server's host key is not checked yet. It showed {fingerprint}: once you are sure the server is yours, put that in Host key.
error.key: The private key is not in OpenSSH or PEM form.
error.key_or_passphrase: The private key or its passphrase is wrong.
error.no_auth: Set a private key or a password.
error.passphrase: The private key has a passphrase: set it in the advanced settings.
error.relative: The directory must be an absolute path: {directory}

field.command_help: Such as systemctl reload nginx; leave it empty for none. It runs in the user's shell.
field.directory_help: An absolute path, such as /etc/nginx/certs, that the user may write to.
field.host_key_help: Proves the server is yours: its SHA256: fingerprint (ssh-keygen -lf /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub on the server shows it), or its line in known_hosts. Left empty, the first deployment fails and shows the server's fingerprint, for you to check and paste here.
field.password_help: To sign in without a key. A key is safer.
field.private_key_help: In OpenSSH or PEM form. Best make JEC a key pair of its own (ssh-keygen -t ed25519) and add the public key to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys of this user on the server. Not shown again once saved.
field.webroot_help: The absolute path the web server serves the domains from, as its root setting says, such as /var/www/html. The user must be able to write there.

layout.by_domain: A subdirectory for each certificate, named after its primary domain

module.description: Writes certificates to a remote server over SSH, then runs a command if set, such as reloading nginx.
module.name: SSH

server.description: Writes the files to a directory on the server as certbot names them, then runs your command. The server needs a POSIX shell, as Linux and BSD have.
server.name: SSH server

test.ok: Signed in to {address} as {user}; the host key matches.
test.webroot_ok: Signed in to {address} as {user}; {directory} can be written to.

webroot.description: Validates domains over HTTP: puts the validation files under /.well-known/ in the website directory of a server reached over SSH, and removes them afterwards. The server needs a POSIX shell.
webroot.name: Website directory over SSH
webroot.per_domain: Each domain has a subdirectory named after it

bot.description: A bot made with @BotFather sends the notes to a person, a group or a channel.
bot.name: Telegram bot

error.api_url: The Bot API server is not a valid address: {url}
error.chat: There is no such chat. Check the chat ID, and message the bot or add it to the group first.
error.forbidden: The bot may not post there: {description}
error.network: Could not reach Telegram. If your network cannot, set a proxy in the advanced settings.
error.proxy: The proxy must start with http://, https:// or socks5://, followed by a host and a port.
error.status: Telegram's answer made no sense (HTTP {status}). Check the Bot API server and the proxy.
error.throttled: Telegram asked to slow down; trying again later.
error.token: Telegram does not accept this bot token. Check it with @BotFather.

field.api_help: Change it only for a Bot API server of your own, or a reverse proxy.
field.chat_help: The number of a person or a group (those of groups and channels start with -100), or @name for a public channel. Message the bot first, add it to the group, or make it an admin of the channel.
field.proxy_help: For a network that cannot reach Telegram, such as http://127.0.0.1:7890 or socks5://127.0.0.1:1080.
field.token_help: @BotFather gives it when you create the bot with /newbot, like 123456:ABC-DEF…

module.description: Sends notes to a chat, a group or a channel through a Telegram bot.
module.name: Telegram

deploy.description: Posts each new version of a certificate, with its private key, as JSON to an HTTPS endpoint of yours, which installs it.
deploy.name: Webhook deployment

error.headers: Not a header: {line}. Write one per line, as Name: value.
error.https: A deployment webhook needs an https:// address, as its requests carry the private key.
error.private: {host} is a private address. To reach it, turn on “Allow private addresses” in the advanced settings.
error.redirect: The endpoint redirects (HTTP {status}) to {location}; use that address instead.

field.allow_private_help: By default only public addresses are reached, so that a webhook cannot probe your network. Turn it on for a receiver on this machine or on your network.
field.deploy_url_help: Must be an https:// address, as the requests carry the private key. The endpoint may answer '{"ref": "…"}', which JEC passes back in previous with the next deployment, so that the old certificate can go.
field.headers_help: One per line, such as Authorization: Bearer xxx. Not shown again once saved.
field.secret_help: When set, each request carries X-JEC-Signature: sha256= and the HMAC-SHA256 of the body with this secret, so the receiver can tell it comes from JEC.
field.url_help: JEC sends it POST requests with JSON bodies.

module.description: Posts notes, or new certificates, to an HTTP endpoint of your own.
module.name: Webhooks

notify.description: Posts each note as JSON to a URL, for any system that takes HTTP requests.
notify.name: Webhook

error.key: WeCom has no robot with this key: it may have been removed. Copy the webhook again.
error.throttled: WeCom asked to slow down (a robot sends at most 20 messages a minute); trying again later.

field.webhook_help: In the WeCom group: its settings → Group Robots → Add. Copy its webhook, which starts with https://qyapi.weixin.qq.com/cgi-bin/webhook/send?key= Anyone who has it can post to the group.

module.description: Sends notes to WeCom (WeChat Work) groups through group robots.
module.name: WeCom

robot.description: A group robot sends the notes to a WeCom group.
robot.name: WeCom robot

answer.description: Validates domains over HTTP, with JEC answering the certificate authority itself. Have the website's reverse proxy (such as nginx) or CDN (such as an origin rule of Alibaba Cloud ESA) send http://the domain/.well-known/ on to JEC.
answer.name: Answered by JEC

error.file_path: The source asked for a file outside /.well-known/, which JEC does not answer: {path}
error.no_domain: Enter a domain to test with first.
error.not_reached: {url} did not answer with JEC's file from the internet. Check that the reverse proxy or CDN sends /.well-known/ on to JEC.

field.domain_help: Testing fetches a temporary file under /.well-known/ of this domain from the internet, to make sure the requests reach JEC.

module.description: JEC answers the validation requests under /.well-known/ itself, which the website's reverse proxy or CDN sends on to it. No access to the website's files is needed.
module.name: Answers from JEC

test.ok: {url} answered from the internet with JEC's file: the requests reach JEC.
